name: Mental Surgery
idea: In the near future a tired office worker goes to a private clinic for mental surgery. He refuses the expensive memory plan. He wakes up delighted with memories he never paid for, and cannot remember upgrading.

cast.name: Martin
cast.description: a man of about 50, a tired office worker: thinning brown hair greying at the temples, soft jaw, pale skin, kind worn eyes; white shirt with the top button undone, grey suit trousers

cast.name: Dr Lane
cast.description: a woman of about 40, calm and immaculate: dark hair in a sleek low bun, fine features, a fixed pleasant customer-service smile; a white high-collared clinic coat

cast.name: Treatment room
cast.description: a near-future private clinic treatment room, quiet and expensive: seamless white walls with soft cove lighting, pale wood floor, one sleek white reclining treatment bed in the centre, a slim glowing ring-shaped halo device on a white arm above the head of the bed, a floor-to-ceiling window with a hazy future city skyline

episodes.title: Mental Surgery
episodes.script:
MENTAL SURGERY

INT. CLINIC TREATMENT ROOM - DAY

A near-future private clinic. MARTIN (about 50, a tired office worker) lies back on a sleek treatment bed under a glowing halo ring. DR LANE (about 40, a fixed customer-service smile) stands beside him with a glass tablet.

MARTIN
I'm ready for my mental surgery.

DR LANE
So. Higher intelligence. French, Spanish, Japanese. And... funnier?

MARTIN
Yes. And add a wild party life in my thirties. And delete the twenty years I spent behind a desk.

DR LANE
Memory editing is Ultra plan only. That's ten thousand dollars a month.

MARTIN
No. Just the basic package.

DR LANE
Of course.

She taps the tablet. The halo lights up. Martin jolts.

INSIDE MARTIN'S MIND

Nanobots rewire glowing neurons. A flash of memory: Martin, twenty years younger, at a beach party at sunset.

INT. CLINIC TREATMENT ROOM - DAY, LATER

Martin sits up, at ease, a different man.

MARTIN
Merci. Gracias. Arigato.
(quietly, to himself)
God, my thirties were good.

DR LANE
And thank you for upgrading to Ultra.

MARTIN
Did I?

DR LANE
You don't remember?

Only Dr Lane is in the frame; Martin is out of frame. Dr Lane's voice: a calm, smooth, warm woman's voice with a neutral American accent, measured and pleasant.

shots.description: Close on Martin's face on the treatment bed as the halo ring above his head lights up bright blue-white and hums. His body jolts once and his eyes go wide. The camera pushes fast into one of his eyes, through the pupil, into darkness filled with glowing neurons. Only Martin is in the frame; Dr Lane is out of frame and no part of her is visible.

takes.endPicture: Inside his brain: a dark space filled with glowing blue neurons and branching connections, with thousands of tiny bright nanobots moving along them and rewiring them, sparks of light where they join. No people, no face.

shots.description: A memory, bright and saturated, not in the clinic: Martin twenty years younger, about 30, with a full head of brown hair, tanned, in an open floral shirt, laughing with his arms in the air in the middle of a crowded beach party at sunset; people dancing around him, confetti in the air, string lights. Fast, joyful, handheld. Loud party music and cheering. Only Martin is in the frame; Dr Lane is out of frame and no part of her is visible.

scenes.heading: INT. CLINIC TREATMENT ROOM - DAY, LATER

shots.description: Deadpan and understated, like a calm customer-service conversation. Martin on the treatment bed, the halo ring now dim. His eyes open. He sits up slowly, at ease, a different man: relaxed shoulders, a small confident smile. Looking towards Dr Lane, he says three thank-yous calmly and fluently, one after another with a short pause between them, each in a perfect native accent: French, then Spanish, then Japanese, with a small polite nod on the last. Then he looks down at his own hands, smiles to himself, and says the last line quietly, almost to himself. Only Martin is in the frame; Dr Lane is out of frame and no part of her is visible. Martin's voice: a soft, tired, mid-low man's voice with a plain English accent, quiet and unhurried.

Deadpan and understated, like a calm customer-service conversation. Dr Lane, warm and pleased, the glass tablet held against her chest, looks at Martin and says her line. Only Dr Lane is in the frame; Martin is out of frame. Dr Lane's voice: a calm, smooth, warm woman's voice with a neutral American accent, measured and pleasant.

dialogue.text: And thank you for upgrading to Ultra.

shots.description: Deadpan and understated, like a calm customer-service conversation. Close on Martin sitting up on the bed. His smile fades into honest puzzlement; he frowns slightly, looks at Dr Lane and asks. Only Martin is in the frame; Dr Lane is out of frame and no part of her is visible. Martin's voice: a soft, tired, mid-low man's voice with a plain English accent, quiet and unhurried.

Deadpan and understated, like a calm customer-service conversation. Very close on Dr Lane's face. Her warm customer-service smile does not move at all. She tilts her head a little and asks softly, then holds the smile. Only Dr Lane is in the frame; Martin is out of frame. Dr Lane's voice: a calm, smooth, warm woman's voice with a neutral American accent, measured and pleasant.

Sleek and minimal: soft glassy synth pads, a slow gentle pulse, a few sparse bell-like notes; polite and soothing like premium hold music, with a faint unsettling undertone that grows slightly towards the end and stops on one unresolved note. Quiet enough to sit under speech. No vocals, no drums.
